page.overview:
What is Woody End?

Woody End was a broad upland forest in the Eastfarthing of the Shire, and west of the Marish.

It was named thus because it occupied the eastern end of the Green-Hill Country, where the green hills became densely filled with trees of all kinds. The woods were sparsely populated and about eight miles in diameter. The Stockbrook and Thistle Brook had their sources in these wooded slopes, and the village of Woodhall was located in the northern eaves.

Woody End was where, after leaving Hobbiton, Frodo, Sam, and Pippin meet a group of Elves led by Gildor; and it was said that one could often meet Elves there.

Later, during the Scouring of the Shire, much smoke spewed out of Woody End due the Ruffians' burning of some of its trees.
